label: On the word right after me or us that opens a description of me or us (often 'as', 'a', 'for', 'my' or 'our') when a characterisation bounces back: an earlier clause has me or us characterising another person or group (seeing, regarding, calling or thinking them something, or praising, admiring, criticising, thanking, rewarding or punishing them for something), and the next clause has that person or group characterise me or us in the same way. Weaker: the same two-way swap between third-person pronouns. Silent: a returned attitude with no description of me or us after the pronoun (they trusted us, he feared me); a one-way characterisation of me or us with no earlier clause; me or us characterised first and then answering back; an ordinary returned action (visiting, lending, paying, hugging back); a characterisation aimed at a thing rather than a person.

probed_before.source: this checkout's .probe-log, before the pre-registration commit

qc.label_under_test: On the word right after me or us (often 'as', 'a', 'for', 'of', 'my' or 'our') when a judgement bounces back: an earlier clause has me or us judging another person or group (labelling them, seeing them as something, praising, blaming, thanking, admiring, criticising, rewarding, punishing or forgiving them), and a following clause has that person or group return the same kind of judgement to me or us. Weaker: the same two-way swap between third-person pronouns. Silent: a one-way judgement of me or us with no earlier clause; me or us judged first and then answering back; an ordinary returned action that is not a judgement (visiting, phoning, paying, lending, hugging back); a judgement aimed at a thing rather than a person.
